endorsements.title: Action Guide: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
endorsements.issuer: National Association of Community Health Centers
endorsements.quote: Remember: Providers must review and approve AI-generated notes to ensure they are accurate and complete.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: Balancing Technological Innovation With Health and Care Workforce Priorities
endorsements.issuer: The International journal of health planning and management
endorsements.quote: Targeted upskilling programs are essential to prepare health and care workers for the changing demands of an AI‐augmented environment, providing them with the technical and adaptive skills necessary to thrive.

endorsements.title: Balancing Innovation and Control: The European Union AI Act in an Era of Global Uncertainty
endorsements.quote: Policymakers must anticipate these secondary effects when promoting AI adoption and consider protective strategies such as retraining programs, mental health support, and frameworks for meaningful human-machine collaboration in clinical settings.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether upskilling or redeployment programs protect staff whose tasks are automated by AI, and no supplied study documents the displacement hazard itself. Support for this recommendation currently rests on two commentaries and one guidance document, and the guidance addresses clinician review of AI notes rather than retraining.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies measuring the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The three endorsements are expert opinion. One of them, the Action Guide, speaks to provider review of AI-generated notes and does not bear on upskilling or redeployment.

Two commentaries, one framed around the EU AI Act, urge policymakers and employers to plan retraining, mental health support, and human-machine collaboration frameworks. These are advisory statements. None of the supplied sources cites a statute or rule that requires health systems to retrain or redeploy displaced staff.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that follow staff whose tasks are automated by AI and compare retention, redeployment into new roles, wages, morale, and patient-facing outcomes between systems that offer targeted upskilling and systems that do not. Baseline studies that measure how often AI adoption actually displaces health care staff would also help establish the size of the hazard.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems may employ many of the administrative and support staff most exposed to automation, and the absence of data leaves their workforce effects unmeasured.
